exposure: Multifetal pregnancy reduction (MFPR) from triplets to twins
conservative management of triplet pregnancies (no intervention)
cohort: The study included 187 triplet pregnancies, with 47 undergoing multifetal pregnancy reduction (MFPR) to twins and 140 managed conservatively.
finding: Multifetal pregnancy reduction (MFPR) in triplet pregnancies significantly prolonged gestational age at delivery, reduced the need for NICU, and improved perinatal prognosis, without increasing maternal complications, compared to conservative management.
mod_finding: Conservative management in triplet pregnancies was an independent risk factor for cesarean delivery (OR 3.4).
gest_age: Gestational age at delivery (35.2 weeks in MFPR group vs 32.2 weeks in conservative management group)
